text:
Nina (Marketing): Quick ask for the launch deck + a short webinar segment. We want a small, reproducible bench that compares generation vs embeddings cost/latency for the same 8k model family. Goal: one slide showing latency vs cost tradeoff and a one-paragraph note on sampling bias.

Nina (Marketing): Request details: 1) run generation (stable-13b-v1, 8k) and embedding (embed-rt-1) on the same sample set of 200 items stratified by prompt length (short/medium/long = 50/100/50). 2) For generation: use max_tokens=128, temp=0.0, seed=123. 3) For embeddings: standard batch size used by SDK. 4) Collect p50/p95/p99 and mean cost-per-1k-tokens and mean cost-per-embedding. 5) Provide a CSV with per-sample latencies + token counts + model variant + quantization flag. Need this by Fri EOD PT (~72h).

Raj (Eng - Runtime): Got it. Clarify: do you want quantized-8 vs fp16 for both gen and embed, or gen only? Also region? Hosted or dedicated?

Nina (Marketing): Prefer both variants where available: quantized-8 for gen, and fp16 baseline for gen; embeddings run on fp16 if quantized embedding kernels unsupported. Region: us-east-1. Hosted (api). Please include any cases where exact parity isn't possible.

Mei (Eng - Runtime): For stratified sample set: do you have canonical text corpus or should we synthesize lengths? If synth, provide RNG seed and length buckets.

Nina (Marketing): Use a mini corpus from the product release notes (we'll attach) but if you need filler, synthesize with seed=2026 and use length buckets: short <=40 chars, medium 200-800 chars, long 2000-5000 chars. Label each row in CSV with bucket.

Arjun (SRE): FYI: we have a maintenance window Fri 02:00-04:00 UTC in us-east-1. Avoid that window for steady-state runs. Also quantized jobs may land on a different pool with slightly different network latencies; we'll annotate that.

Raj (Eng - Runtime): Plan: create the stratified payload list (200 items), run coldstart cohort (fresh container) 20 samples per variant to capture startup behavior, then steady-state: 2 RPS for 6 minutes and 50 RPS for 6 minutes. For embeddings, run typical batch sizes and a high-throughput batch sim at 200 qps for 3 minutes. We'll capture token-level breakdown where applicable and collect 25 raw traces per run (headers + waterfall).

Raj (Eng - Runtime): Repro commands we'll include in README. Example snippet for generation:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"stable-13b-v1","input":"<text>","max_tokens":128,"temperature":0.0,"seed":123}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Mei (Eng - Runtime): We'll also produce a delta CSV showing variance decomposition across prompt length, quantization, and traffic level. That should help marketing justify the messaging about typical vs tail behavior.

ci-bot: ci-bot: scheduled bench job #5902 queued in us-east-1 (quantized-8).

Nina (Marketing): Awesome. In the README please include: exact SDK/curl commands, RNG seeds, definition of coldstart vs warm (how many primes), any observed non-determinism, and the S3 path for artifacts. Also one short suggested bullet for the slide: "embedding calls are ~X ms cheaper on average but gen latency dominates when using long context" (we'll edit X with your number).

Raj (Eng - Runtime): ETA: Fri 16:00 PT. If SRE window or pool contention hits, fallback Fri 22:00 PT. We'll upload a zip: artifacts.csv (per-sample), raw_traces/, README.md, and cost_estimates.csv. We'll note limitations: e.g., embedding quant kernels inconsistent across instance types.

Nina (Marketing): Thanks! If you spot systematic bias in our synthetic long prompts, call it out in-thread so we can tweak the messaging. :memo:
